leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations contain a single B041 part naming Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, with citations centred on GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide form that enabled incretin-based therapy. Shared: a complete arc from hormone physiology to large independent outcome trials, and a view that timing is not premature. Not shared or unresolved: each member names Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's exclusion as the main cost; members differ on how to describe that exclusion (Sandberg and Linnarsson place her work on the product side of the line, while Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson say it should not be dismissed as merely industrial); and no member can verify Mojsov's priority for the active peptide or the claims of contributors outside the credited list such as Habener. Five members would not displace any of the three names for Knudsen at present; Perlmann and Sandberg would reopen the question only if the citation were framed around the drugs.

areas_of_agreement: All six members place B041 in their preferred configuration with the same three laureates, and each states that the case rests on the science rather than on the unanimity of opening ranks.
Every member names attribution, specifically the exclusion of Knudsen under the three-person limit and the uncertain priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, as the main weakness of B041.
B030 (CAR-T) is named as an alternative by all six members; none prefers it to B041, and none disputes its clinical maturity.

Narrowing B030 to June and Sadelain is described as more defensible than the three-name credit by Perlmann (who proposes it) and, in their responses, by El-Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson; the originators of the chimeric receptor concept (e.g. Eshhar) are outside the credited names.
No member would let an unverified concern about a person's standing (raised for Sabatini in B011) shape attribution; credit should follow the documented scientific record.
B035 (unfolded protein response, Mori and Walter) is described by several members as the cleanest two-person allocation among the basic-mechanism candidates, though none places it above B041.
scientific_disputes: Whether the B041 citation should rest on physiology and identification of the active peptide, or whether the essential achievement is the long-acting drug design, which would change which three names are central.

Whether optogenetics (B039) fits a discovery prize: El-Manira and Wahren-Herlenius keep it as an alternative; Wahren-Herlenius notes the Nobel tradition has honoured methods that opened new biology, while El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson stress that it is a research tool with early clinical effect.

Whether mechanistic clarity (B035) should weigh against direct clinical consequence (B030, B023): Svenningsson and Linnarsson keep B035 as an alternative, Wahren-Herlenius and Sandberg would place CAR-T and optogenetics or CAR-T and GLP-1 ahead of it, and Perlmann ranks B023 above it.

Whether TOR signalling (B011) is conceptually foundational but too diffuse clinically (Linnarsson, Svenningsson) or attribution-limited (Perlmann, El-Manira), and whether a Hall and Schreiber pairing under-credits the mTORC1 mechanistic work.
attribution_disputes: B041: with four credited names and three places, whether Knudsen should displace one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, and if so which of the three is least central; no member has proposed a specific displacement.

B041: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is described as contested by every member who addresses it, and none can resolve it from the supplied material; Habener is raised as an early contributor outside the credited list by El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius.

B030: whether Rosenberg belongs with June and Sadelain; Linnarsson would not dismiss his adoptive transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials as clinical proof of concept, while Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius treat his work as a broader cell-therapy lineage.

B039: six credited names against three places; the trios proposed by El-Manira and Wahren-Herlenius (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) omit Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, and Sandberg moved toward that trio from an opening that favoured Boyden over Hegemann.
B011: whether Hall and Schreiber are the core pairing and whether Sabatini's exclusion can be justified on scientific grounds alone.
maturity_disputes: B041 is described by all members as mature, independently confirmed and at peak impact; the only timing argument recorded is Sandberg's observation that waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit question cannot be resolved, because CAR-T is equally mature.

B035: the mechanism is mature, but Perlmann, Linnarsson, El-Manira and Wahren-Herlenius say the translational thread (integrated stress response, ISRIB-type compounds) is still developing; El-Manira adds that omitting Ron's PERK and CHOP work leaves a visible gap.
B039: widely adopted as a tool, but its clinical effect is characterised as early by Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson.

B023: Perlmann treats BCR-ABL inhibition as very mature and overdue; El-Manira accepts maturity but doubts a clean three-person split given prior chromosomal and kinase biology and industrial chemistry.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses roughly twenty co-authored works with Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard; he reports no relation to B041, B030 or B035 or their credited names.

Perlmann discloses the same co-authorship with Svenningsson, a 2009 co-authored paper with El-Manira, and past nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans (not a credited name on the shortlist); he reports none bearing on a shortlisted candidate.
El-Manira discloses the 2009 paper with Perlmann and a past collaboration with Grillner, and notes that his circuit-neuroscience field is adjacent to B039.
Linnarsson notes that optogenetics (B039) is adjacent to his field and that his documented co-authorship in spatial transcriptomics and brain atlases concerns work outside the shortlist.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen and shared institution with colleagues, none connected to a shortlisted candidate.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that B026 (TNF blockade) and B031 (cGAS-STING) are close to her field, that neither is in her preferred configuration, and that she will recuse if a documented co-author or close institutional tie emerges.
questions_for_round2: Should the B041 citation be anchored in physiology and identification of the active peptide, and if the committee instead names drug design, which of Drucker, Holst and Mojsov would give way to Knudsen and on what documented grounds?

What evidence in the supplied record bears on Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and on the roles of Habener and other contributors outside the credited list, and does any of it change the three-name allocation?
Is a single-achievement prize for B041 preferable to a two-part prize, bearing in mind that a second part would require cutting B041 to two names or a second part limited to one or two names?
If a second part is wanted, is B030 limited to June and Sadelain the most defensible candidate, and how should the absence of the chimeric receptor originators such as Eshhar be treated?
Should Rosenberg be included in any B030 configuration, and on what specific CAR-related or clinical proof-of-concept grounds?
Does a research tool (B039) belong in a discovery prize at this stage, and if so, which three of the six credited names would a citation name and why?
Between mechanistic clarity with clean attribution (B035) and demonstrated clinical effect (B030, B023), which criterion should decide the strongest alternative to B041?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on a single preferred B041 configuration and on the same weakness, the cut among four credited names and the unverified priority for the active peptide. Disagreement concerns which alternative is next strongest (B030 in all six files, B039 in three, B035 in two, B023 in one), how narrowly to credit B030, and whether tools or mechanism-only discoveries fit the prize. Only positions stated in the six files are counted here, and none of these points has been resolved.
